q: A supplier's late delivery is stopping the team's work today. How should the project manager classify this?
options: A risk, since it might affect the schedule later
An issue, since it is happening now
An assumption to record in the assumption log
A lesson learned for the next project only
explanation: An issue is a current condition that has already occurred and may need immediate action. A risk is uncertain and in the future.

q: Which document records the project's issues, with their owners, priorities and target resolution dates?
options: The risk register
The assumption log
The stakeholder register
The issue log
explanation: The issue log is the project document where information about issues is recorded and monitored.

q: An identified risk, that the main crane may break down, has just occurred. A response was planned. What should the project manager do?
options: Treat it as an issue and carry out the planned response
Leave it in the risk register as a future threat
Wait for the risk review at the end of the month
Close the risk register entry and do nothing else at all
explanation: A risk that occurs is no longer uncertain: it becomes an issue. Implement Risk Responses executes the agreed response and updates the issue log and risk register.

q: A developer has been blocked for three days waiting for test data from another department. What should the team's supportive leader do?
options: Tell the developer to work around the rules for now
Take over the developer's other tasks personally
Work with that department to remove the blocker
Wait for the next retrospective to discuss the delay at length
explanation: Supportive leaders remove organizational impediments, working with departments whose processes slow the team, so the team can keep delivering.

q: Every finished increment then waits six weeks in another department's release queue. What does the Agile Practice Guide expect the leader to do?
options: Ask the team to slow down to match the release queue
Work with that department to streamline the process
Stop delivering increments until the queue clears up completely
Release the product without the department's approval
explanation: Lengthy release processes are bottlenecks; the supportive leader partners with others to review their processes and can change or remove these organizational impediments.

q: How do team members typically raise impediments in iteration-based agile?
options: In a written report to the sponsor each month
Only in the retrospective at the end of the iteration
By email to the PMO, which assigns an owner
In the daily meeting: 'What are my impediments?'
explanation: In iteration-based agile, everyone answers what they completed, what they plan to complete, and what their impediments (or risks or problems) are.

q: The team's impediments are discussed but never written down, and several get forgotten. What should the project manager introduce?
options: A visible impediment list with severity and actions
A rule that only the leader may mention impediments in meetings
A monthly report of impediments to the board
A ban on discussing impediments in daily meetings
explanation: Visual controls can include an impediment list showing each impediment, its severity and the actions being taken to resolve it.

q: Team members hide blocked work because they fear being blamed. What is the underlying problem?
options: The team has too many tasks on its board
The iterations are too long for the work
Low psychological safety in the team
The product owner is not prioritizing the backlog well
explanation: With psychological safety, team members raise impediments immediately, ask for help and swarm on blocked work without fear of blame.

q: Three impediments compete for the project manager's time. How should they be handled?
options: In the order in which they were reported to the team
By priority, based on their impact on objectives
All at the same time, with equal effort on each
The cheapest one to fix first, whatever its impact on the project
explanation: Evaluate each impediment's impact and prioritize; the issue log records a priority for each issue so the most damaging get attention first.

q: A recurring build failure blocks the team every week, and fixing it takes a day each time. What should the team do?
options: Keep fixing it each week as it appears
Accept it as a normal part of the work
Ask the sponsor for more developers to absorb the delay
Find and remove the root cause of the failure
explanation: Root cause analysis determines the basic reason for a problem; when all root causes are removed, the problem does not recur.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Root cause analysis

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Root cause analysis

q: The team cannot size a story because the technical approach is unknown. Which intervention fits?
options: Timebox a spike to learn what is needed
Assign the story to the most senior developer to just build it
Skip the story and never return to it
Ask the sponsor to choose the approach
explanation: When a team struggles with obstacles, the Agile Practice Guide suggests empowering impediment escalation, timeboxing spikes and swarming on systemic blockers.

q: Which of these impediments is most clearly one the team cannot remove on its own?
options: A missing unit test in the code
Two members disagreeing on a design detail
A company policy requiring a monthly approval
A story that needs splitting into smaller parts
explanation: Organizational processes such as approvals, finance, change control boards and audits are organizational impediments; a leader works with those owners to change them.

q: Resolving an issue needs extra budget beyond the project manager's authority. What should happen?
options: Approve the budget personally to save time
Escalate it along the agreed path
Leave it unresolved until the next phase
Ask the team to vote on the extra budget at its next meeting
explanation: Escalation is useful where decision authority lies outside the team or with higher-ranking people who can remove persistent obstacles.

q: In larger agile delivery settings, what does the Agile Practice Guide say project managers may often do?
options: Assign the tasks to each team member every single morning
Replace the product owners on every team
Write all of the user stories for the teams
Escalate and remove organization-level impediments
explanation: Project managers may move into external-facing coordination roles: aligning teams and dependencies, escalating and removing organization-level impediments, and guiding teams through enterprise processes.

q: Which data does the Sixth Edition list for an issue in the issue log?
options: Priority, assignee, target date and final solution
Probability, impact, trigger and the risk owner
Story points, velocity and iteration number
Contract type, fee and the agreed payment schedule
explanation: The issue log may include issue type, who raised it and when, description, priority, who is assigned, target resolution date, status and final solution.

q: Ambiguity about a requirement is slowing the team, but it has not become a risk. What does the PMBOK Guide suggest?
options: Add it to the risk register as a high risk
Escalate it to the sponsor at once
Resolve it through collaborative problem-solving
Ignore it until it becomes an issue later in the project
explanation: Ambiguous and uncertain situations do not always escalate into risks; as information arrives and experts get involved, they can often be resolved through collaborative problem-solving.

q: Which processes update the issue log as risks turn into issues?
options: Develop Schedule and Estimate Costs
Implement Risk Responses and Monitor Risks
Plan Scope Management and Define Scope
Identify Stakeholders and Plan Communications Management
explanation: Figures 2-52 and 2-53 list issue log updates among the outputs of Implement Risk Responses and Monitor Risks.

q: A retrospective produces twelve action items to remove impediments. What is a good next step?
options: Assign all twelve to the scrum master
Drop all of them, as there are too many
Wait until the next project to act on any of them
Pick the most important and follow through
explanation: A team may end up with many action items to remove impediments; it chooses the most important to act on and follows through.

q: Two stakeholders disagree on how an issue should be resolved. What should the project manager do first?
options: Bring them together to work on the approach
Pick the solution of the more senior one
Escalate it straight to the board
Leave the issue open until they agree on their own, however long it takes
explanation: The enabler is to collaborate with relevant stakeholders on an approach. The Code also asks us to approach those in a conflict directly first.

q: For how long does the issue log stay in use on a project?
options: Only during the initiating phase
Only until the first issue is resolved
Throughout the project, updated by monitoring
Only in projects that use an agile approach for delivery
explanation: Issues may happen at any time; the issue log is updated as a result of monitoring and controlling throughout the life cycle.

q: Which Agile Practice Guide suggestion helps with unexpected or unforeseen delays?
options: Add more work in process to keep everyone busy
Visualize blockers and limit work in process
Lengthen feedback loops to reduce interruptions
Stop holding daily coordination meetings for a while
explanation: For unexpected delays: visualize blockers, run delay diagnostics, limit WIP and shorten feedback loops.

q: A negative risk has occurred. What is the scheduling standard's term for the response to it?
options: A contingency reserve
A risk threshold
A risk trigger
A workaround
explanation: A workaround is a response to a negative risk that has occurred. A trigger signals that a risk is about to occur; a reserve is time or money, not a response.

q: How should the steel delay now be handled?
options: As an issue, carrying out the second-supplier plan
As a new risk to analyze at the next review
As a lesson learned for future bridges
As a change request to reduce the bridge's scope and size
explanation: The identified risk has occurred, so it is now an issue; the planned contingency response is carried out and the issue log and risk register are updated.

q: What should the project manager do about the safety permit?
options: Tell the crew to start work without the permit
Contact the traffic department to clear the blocker
Wait until the department contacts the project
Move the night crew permanently to another city project
explanation: The permit is an impediment the crew cannot remove; the leader works with the department that owns the process. Working without a required permit would break compliance.

q: How should the disagreement about the pour sequence be resolved?
options: Let the foreman decide alone, since the crew does the pour work
Escalate it to the city council at once
Bring both together with the facts to agree an approach
Postpone the pour until the project ends
explanation: Collaborate with the relevant stakeholders on an approach; subject matter experts and the facts turn disagreement into a decision. Escalate only if it is beyond the project's authority.

q: Which TWO describe an issue rather than a risk?
options: It has already occurred
It may need immediate action
It may or may not happen
It is written as cause, event and consequence
It is assessed by its probability
explanation: An issue has occurred or is occurring and may need immediate action or management attention. Uncertainty, probability and the cause-event-consequence structure describe risks.

q: Which THREE are ways a supportive leader removes or reduces impediments, according to the Agile Practice Guide?
options: Working with departments to streamline slow processes
Exposing bottlenecks so the teams can resolve them
Escalating organization-level impediments
Doing the team's technical work for it
Making the team's decisions for it
Hiding impediments from stakeholders
explanation: Leaders facilitate (expose bottlenecks so teams resolve them), remove organizational impediments, and in larger settings escalate organization-level impediments. They do not make decisions others are responsible for.

q: Which TWO belong in an impediment list on a visual control?
options: The severity of each impediment
The actions being taken to resolve it
The team members' salaries
The project's full budget
The vendor's contract terms
explanation: An impediment list shows a description of each impediment, its severity, and the actions being taken to resolve it.

q: Match each situation with a fitting intervention.
left: A defect that keeps coming back
A decision beyond the project manager's authority
right: The leader works with that department
explanation: The team solves what it can (spikes, root causes); leaders remove organizational impediments; escalation handles what is beyond the project's authority.

q: Complete each statement about impediments and issues.

blanks.text: An obstacle that prevents the team from reaching its objectives is an
A current condition that may affect one or more objectives is an
A response to a negative risk that has occurred is a

explanation: Impediments block the team; issues have already happened; workarounds respond to risks that have occurred.
